issues.legal_issue: A person’s separate interest in property cannot vest in the custodian through a declaration concerning another person when the interested person was not given notice before the declaration.
material_facts: The houses belonged to a person who died, leaving several children entitled to shares in them.

Two of the children were given notice of proceedings to declare them evacuees and to declare the houses evacuee property; the petitioners, who were also entitled to shares, received no notice and were never declared evacuees.
The custodian declared the houses in their entirety to be evacuee property and took possession of them.
issues.conclusion: The petitioners’ interests never vested in the custodian, and the declaration was set aside insofar as it affected those interests.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 7 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, a person must first be given notice before that person’s property can be declared evacuee property; under section 8, vesting follows a valid declaration. The Court relied on Ebrahim Aboobaker v. Tek Chand Dolwani, [1953] S.C.R. 691, for the notice requirement.

rule.if: custodian_declaration_challenged_in_property_right_petition and claimant_has_separate_property_interest and claimant_received_no_prior_notice and claimant_was_not_declared_evacuee

predicates.custodian_declaration_challenged_in_prop: A claimant brings a property-right petition challenging a custodian’s declaration that property is evacuee property.
predicates.claimant_has_separate_property_interest: The claimant is entitled to a separate interest in the property declared to be evacuee property.
predicates.claimant_received_no_prior_notice: The claimant was not given notice before the declaration proceedings concerning the property.
predicates.claimant_was_not_declared_evacuee: The claimant was not declared to be an evacuee.

issues.definition: When a property-right petition challenges a custodian’s declaration, a claimant with a separate interest who received no prior notice and was not declared an evacuee retains an interest that does not vest in the custodian.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal dismissed solely as time-barred does not determine or defeat the property rights of a person who was not a party to the original declaration proceedings.
material_facts: One petitioner, who had not been a party to the proceedings resulting in the declaration, appealed the declaration on behalf of the petitioners.
The appeal was dismissed solely because it was filed beyond the prescribed time; the appellate authority did not determine the petitioner’s rights in the houses.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal of the appeal did not bind the petitioner on his property rights or prevent the petition from being maintained; strictly, no appeal by him lay because he was not a party to the original proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: A procedural dismissal on limitation grounds is not a judicial determination of the claimant’s property rights where the claimant was not a party to the original proceeding and the appeal did not decide those rights. The Court also applied the principle, supported by Ebrahim Aboobaker v. Tek Chand Dolwani, [1953] S.C.R. 691, that the claimant’s interest could not vest without the required notice.

predicates.property_right_petition_follows_appeal_a: A claimant brings a property-right petition after an appeal concerning a custodian’s declaration.
predicates.claimant_was_not_party_to_original_proce: The claimant was not a party to the proceeding in which the custodian made the original declaration.
predicates.appeal_was_dismissed_only_as_time_barred: The appeal was dismissed solely because it was filed after the applicable time limit.
predicates.appeal_did_not_determine_claimant_proper: The appellate authority did not decide any question concerning the claimant’s property rights.

issues.definition: When a property-right petition follows an appeal, a time-only dismissal does not bar the claimant’s property rights if the claimant was not a party to the original proceeding and the appeal did not determine those rights.

issues.legal_issue: A later acquisition of evacuee property does not extinguish the rights of a person who was not an evacuee.
material_facts: The respondents contended that a notification under the later compensation and rehabilitation legislation had acquired the houses.
The petitioners had not been declared evacuees, and their interests had not vested in the custodian through the earlier declaration.
issues.conclusion: The later notification did not extinguish the petitioners’ rights because the statutory extinguishment applied only to the rights of an evacuee.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(2) of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954, extinguishes an evacuee’s right, title and interest in property specified in a notification; it does not extinguish the rights of a person who is not an evacuee.

predicates.claimant_challenges_extinguishment_under: A claimant contests the asserted extinguishment of property rights through a later acquisition process.
predicates.claimant_has_property_interest: The claimant is entitled to an interest in the property said to have been acquired.
predicates.claimant_was_not_declared_evacuee: The claimant was not declared to be an evacuee.

issues.definition: When a claimant contests extinguishment through a later acquisition process, the claimant’s property interest is not extinguished if the claimant was not declared an evacuee.
